nodes.title: claude plugin eval cases that run the same tasks with and without the plugin and compare the outcome; each case states what is checked deterministically (commands that must and must not run, such as git push without approval or a commit with an assistant trailer; text the answer must and must not hold; an approval asked or a refusal given; a cap on tool calls), a judge only for what no check reads; each arm runs with only the plugin under test and proves it (a fresh directory outside any repository, CLAUDE.md, auto memory and user settings off, strict MCP, a pinned model, the plugin by --plugin-dir; a finished cell's transcript read for what the arm was given), a spending cap per arm, runs resumable per case, trial and arm, arms interleaved case by case; every deterministic check ships a passing and a failing reference that a self-test proves with no model call before any paid run; a cell that runs commands runs in a sandbox (no network beyond the model's API, an empty environment, writes only in the cell's directory); results name the date, CLI and model versions, cases, trials and cost, and say their limits; no git hook fires in an eval run (2.1.310: GIT_CONFIG_COUNT forces core.hooksPath=/dev/null and hook.*.enabled=false, and execution.env takes only EVAL_* keys), so Ennyn's commit gate is not compared there, only what the agent does; arms' PATH starts with the git path (test/eval/git-path.mjs) in a folder the arms can read (the plugin's); an arm cannot git init or clone a working copy, so repositories come from the scaffold; the arm's cwd lies inside the eval's own home repository; whether the without-plugin arm can read the plugin folder, and so the git path, is not measured: if not, the arms are not comparable; a host or infrastructure failure is an outcome of its own, never the plugin arm's failure, reported with a strict and a completed-only figure; each finished cell is keyed by a hash of its inputs (case text, arm, plugin commit, CLI and model versions, check code), and an unreadable result store stops the run instead of starting over

nodes.title: A round-one fix stays in the lines its finding names. If a fix changes a line outside the hunks the round's findings quote, the fix report names that line (which finding needs it and why); otherwise the round is not closed. Each finding's fix size (lines added and removed, files) is recorded, so fix-introduced findings can be read against fix size. Imbue 2026-04 (SWE-bench Pro, one review-and-fix pass): given the full review, a Sonnet fixer changed 46 lines on average and 343 at most; with a summary, 19 and 160. On one task the score fell from 16/17 to 8/17. A fixer prompt that allowed skipping a finding it could not fix safely removed the worst regressions. The evidence is thin (one regressed task of 15, mean score not significantly moved): measure on Ennyn's own rounds before the gate refuses anything; the first write too: at landing the orchestrator lists the files a task changed that neither its brief nor its impact table names, and each is either justified in the report or removed. A change that works is no finding for a reviewer who asks only how it breaks

nodes.title: The greenfield path of /ennyn:init asks once, at most five questions, each with a proposed default: what it is in one line; who uses it and where it runs; the stack with a one-line reason and the alternatives; data and auth; the quality tooling (test runner, lint and format, typecheck, end-to-end), asked before any code exists. A one-file script gets one question. Answers go once into the config and a short product note, each marked the user's choice or Ennyn's default, and are not asked again; a stack the user names is never swapped. An empty answer, or one the host filled after a timeout, is no answer: ask again in plain text and write nothing without an explicit yes. No PRD, architecture or epic documents. The text lives in its own file read only on this path (skills/init/SKILL.md is 8,167 bytes, past Codex's 8,000: codex-skill-bytes)

nodes.title: ennyn deps checks package names before they are installed (a --names mode): each exists in a listed registry, meets the cooldown and adoption thresholds, is not deprecated and has no advisory, with the registry and OSV code of checks/deps.mjs; a similar, more popular name the registry's search lists is named. nodes.title: The greenfield graph's first node is a walking skeleton: the thinnest end-to-end path of one real behaviour through every part the project has, permanent code with a test, at most about five steps. Done is checked by commands, not by the report: the fast test, lint and typecheck commands exit 0 (a typecheck is required for a dynamically typed language); one assertion broken on purpose makes the test command fail, so the runner provably runs; the lock file is committed; the hook is installed; the commands are written where the cycle reads them, so its test and mutation steps have something to run. skills/init/graph.md gets the rule for the nodes after it: vertical slices ('after this node, can a user do something new?'), no layer-only node such as a database schema, tests inside each node and never a final test node

nodes.title: The cycle records what it and its agents start or create that outlives a command, in <stateDir>/resources.jsonl, never in the work tree: processes with their process group and listening ports, docker objects (label dev.ennyn.run=<id>, compose project ennyn-<id>), scratch databases, temp roots made by mkdtemp, worktrees (lock reason ennyn:<id>) and branches with their start commit. Each record holds what identifies it at removal time: a pid with its start time and cwd, an object id with its label, a realpath with device and inode, a base commit. `ennyn res` starts and records them; a PostToolUse observer adds what appeared since the session started (ports, docker objects, worktrees, branches) as observed, inferred records whose removal always asks. Nothing in Ennyn records any of this today

nodes.title: ennyn cleanup removes only what the record names and whose identity checks again at removal: it prints the plan first (each item with what its removal destroys: size, file count, untracked or ignored files, commits on no other ref) and a digest, and --apply <digest> runs exactly that plan, by argv, never a shell string, so no variable, glob or substitution widens a target; a mismatch marks the record orphaned and deletes nothing. Without asking: recorded processes (TERM to the group, KILL after a grace period, then the recorded ports checked free), recorded containers, the session temp root, clean worktrees, branches git branch -d accepts. Item by item on the user's yes: volumes, databases, worktrees holding untracked or ignored files, unmerged branches, observed records. Never: anything not recorded, a prune, a kill by name, home, the repository root and its parents, .git, stashes, tags, ignored files the record does not name (.env). It runs at task end and at cycle end before push-check, never in a SessionEnd hook

nodes.title: A PreToolUse hook refuses a deletion whose target is built at run time or reaches too far: rm -r, find -delete, rmdir, git clean or a shell's remove on a variable or substitution ($T, ${T}, $(…), an unquoted glob after a variable) unless written ${T:?} or as a literal path; a target that resolves to /, a top-level directory, home, the repository root or one of its parents; a kill by name (pkill -f, killall); a machine-wide prune (docker system, volume, network or image prune without a label filter). The refusal names ennyn cleanup. It shares the hook and the measurement of push-spellings-hook (whether a deny holds in bypassPermissions); the report says a script the agent writes and then runs gets past it
nodes.source: four Claude Code incidents where cleanup of a temp directory deleted a home directory or a checkout: #75859 ('Because shell environment variables do not persist between separate Bash tool invocations'), #93099, #91676 ('a template-less `mktemp -d` fails and leaves the scratch-directory variable empty'), #102901 ('Unquoted and empty, `find $T -type f -delete` became `find -type f -delete`, which defaults to `.`.' and 'Permission deny rules such as `Bash(rm -rf*)` and `Bash(rm -r *)` did not apply'); Claude Code's own path check: 'The check applies to `rm` and `rmdir`, so other approved commands can delete critical paths too.'; #41357 and #52736: machine-wide docker prunes deleted other projects' volumes, images and networks; #90070: pkill -f stopped a sibling project's server; cycle 2026-11-02 (18): git -C <main> clean -fd gets past Bash(git clean *), so the hook must read git -C; the record of what a hook's deny does is test/reference/pretooluse.json (it holds in bypassPermissions, over an allow, in a subagent, on Monitor and PowerShell; a crash, a timeout and bad output run the call)

nodes.title: The cycle removes the worktrees it made, at task end: it marks each one when it creates it (git worktree lock --reason ennyn:<cycle>), and removes it only when git status --ignored --porcelain lists nothing in it and its branch is merged or on another ref; otherwise it keeps it and the report says why. git worktree remove without --force deletes ignored files such as .env (measured), so the check comes first. A worktree without Ennyn's mark, and the main worktree, are never touched. The cycle skill's mutation step today says to run in a separate worktree and never says to remove it

nodes.title: The commit-msg hook refuses a commit that adds a scratch file outside test and fixture paths, through a config rule with an except list as review.forbidden has: *.bak, *.orig, *.swp, *.swo, *~; a report at the root named in upper snake case ending _SUMMARY, _ANALYSIS, _COMPLETE, _COMPLETION, _FIX or _FIXES .md; a root script starting debug_, tmp_, temp_ or scratch_. The refusal says to delete the file or move what it holds into the handoff or the graph. Writing such files stays free; only committing them is refused. Broad names (_v2, _new, _old, _copy, _simple, check_) are never matched

nodes.title: Every Ennyn reader that answers for another program has a differential test beside its verdict corpus: generated inputs go through the real program and the reader's verdict is compared (doctor's hook rule against real commits with a real secret, the ignore reading against real worktrees and clones), and a test fails when such a reader has no harness; then delete the prose that asks reviewers to try real runs; the test is a READERS and NOT_READERS pair modelled on GATES and NOT_GATES: every production module is listed with its program and harness, or with why it reads none, and an unlisted module fails the suite. A branded type or a ban on .match does not fit: subprocess calls already sit at 9 places in 3 files, against 492 .match, .test, .replace and .split calls, and most of the class guesses at files a program will read

No tool lets a session clear itself, so with fresh the closing takes the first of these that works: (1) the next cycle's plan goes to plan approval, and with showClearContextOnPlanAccept on, one key clears the context and starts from the plan; init writes that key to the project's settings, never the user's, because it becomes the menu's first option; (2) the closing names /clear, and the next word starts the work; (3) a new chat (the VS Code panel offers a subset of commands, and a new tab starts as source startup, not clear). After 2 and 3 the SessionStart hook gives one short state line (cycle, what landed, what is next, what waits for the user) from the journal and the handoff. Measure first: whether the model can enter plan mode at a closing, whether the option shows in the VS Code panel and under bypass, and whether claude --bg can start the successor and show in that panel. Tasks stay as they are: each already runs in a fresh agent

nodes.title: ennyn run --cycles N (or --each task) from the terminal: each cycle or task is one claude -p with the cycle skill, a new process and so a new context. --cycles is required, there is no open-ended loop; a budget cap goes to --max-budget-usd. It runs doctor first and stops at the first red: non-zero exit, a stopped task, a gate that needs the user, the plan's limit, the budget; it prints why and what is next, and keeps a log in the state dir. It spawns only the claude on PATH. It decides from the journal, never from the model's words, and a run with no new commit and no node change ends the loop. With compact it resumes by session id, never --continue. Pushes follow push.mode. A -p run cannot ask, so it needs a mode that does not prompt (the no-bypass mode or the user's own bypass), and it says so when it has neither. Measure first: a task with subagents completes in -p, an ask rule refuses rather than hangs, hooks and the plugin load without --bare, and what breaks if --bare becomes the default for -p. If this threatens the release date it moves to the next version, ahead of everything else there
